scenes.heading: Variation and natural selection
scenes.sub: Why do populations change over generations?
scenes.say: No two people in your class look exactly alike, and the same goes for kangaroos, gum trees and bacteria. Those differences are the raw material for evolution.

scenes.heading: Two kinds of variation

right.title: Discontinuous
points: Often one or a few genes

scenes.say: Continuous variation is like a ramp: height can be any value. Discontinuous variation is like a staircase: blood group falls into clear groups. Only variation caused by genes can be passed on, so only that matters for evolution.

scenes.heading: Sources of genetic variation
points: Mutation: the only source of new alleles
scenes.say: Mutation is the only way brand-new alleles appear. Most mutations are neutral or harmful, and a few help. Sexual reproduction then shuffles existing alleles through independent assortment, crossing over and random fertilisation. That's why siblings look different.

scenes.heading: Very Strong Dogs Inherit Change
scenes.say: Darwin and Wallace explained natural selection. Remember: Very Strong Dogs Inherit Change. Variation, selection pressure, differential survival and reproduction, inheritance, and change over generations, as the helpful allele becomes more common.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Hide and seek: kids in well-camouflaged clothes last longest
scenes.science: Birds eat fewer well-camouflaged moths, so that form becomes common
scenes.breaks: kids can choose to change clothes, but organisms can't. The variation must already exist before the selection pressure arrives.
scenes.say: Think of hide and seek, where kids already wear different colours. The seeker is like birds hunting peppered moths. When soot blackened tree trunks, dark moths were harder to see and became common. The moths didn't change colour. Birds simply ate more of the easy-to-see form.

scenes.heading: What 'fittest' really means
points: Fitness = how many offspring you leave
scenes.say: Survival of the fittest doesn't mean the strongest wins. Fitness is how many offspring you leave, a bit like how many times a post gets shared. And individuals don't evolve. They survive or die, while the population changes.

scenes.heading: Data question
scenes.question: Same insecticide every year. Beetles surviving a test spray (of 100): year 1: 2, year 3: 15, year 5: 48, year 7: 81. Explain.
lines: A few beetles already had a resistance allele
Resistant ones bred and passed it on
The spray selected, it didn't cause it
scenes.say: Beetles surviving a spray rose from two to eighty-one out of a hundred in seven years. A few already carried a resistance allele. The spray killed the rest, and the survivors passed it on. Don't say the beetles got used to it. The spray selected resistance that was already there.
scenes.caption: Beetles surviving a spray rose from 2 to 81 out of 100 in seven years. A few already carried a resistance allele. The spray killed the rest, and the survivors passed it on. Don't say the beetles got used to it. The spray selected resistance that was already there.

scenes.say: Quick recap. Mutation makes new alleles and sex shuffles them. Selection acts on variation that's already there. Fitness means offspring, and populations evolve, not individuals. Now try the practice questions!
